question: Can a differentiable loss make a low-dimensional representation preserve not only the persistence of topological features in the source data but also where those features are localized?

key_findings.claim: Representation Topology Divergence compares two corresponding point clouds through cross-barcode constructions, penalizing disagreements in both the existence and localization of persistent topological features.
key_findings.evidence: The paper forms a coupled distance construction over source and representation points, defines a directed R-Cross-Barcode discrepancy and symmetrizes it into RTD, then proves that vanishing discrepancies in both directions force the relevant persistence barcodes and representative feature locations to agree.

key_findings.claim: RTD can be differentiated almost everywhere and added to an autoencoder objective, giving a practical topology-aware representation learner rather than only a post-hoc diagnostic.
key_findings.evidence: RTD-AE evaluates persistence on mini-batches, differentiates selected filtration edges back through pairwise distances, and optimizes reconstruction plus an RTD regularizer. A reconstruction warm start is used because direct joint optimization is otherwise unstable and expensive.

key_findings.claim: Across synthetic manifolds and several image, object, and single-cell datasets, RTD-AE is usually among the strongest methods on global metric and topological preservation, but it is not uniformly best on every dimensionality and metric.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments on nested spheres, Mammoth, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, COIL-20, and scRNA-seq compare correlation, triplet accuracy, barcode Wasserstein distance, and RTD against PCA/MDS, t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP, PHATE, ivis, a plain autoencoder, and TopoAE. RTD-AE is especially strong in 16 dimensions, while PCA, TopoAE, or another visualization method wins selected 2-D or individual-metric cases.

key_findings.claim: The stronger topology guarantee carries a material computational price and is normally restricted to degree-one homology in training.
key_findings.evidence: The authors report pairwise-distance work quadratic in mini-batch size and persistence computation with a much worse worst case; measured overhead grows from about 1.5 times a basic autoencoder at batch size 8 to roughly 4--6 times at batch size 512. Higher-dimensional homology is described as expensive and often low-signal for the tested data, so most optimization targets loops rather than arbitrary-dimensional features.

method.core_idea: Compare source and latent metric spaces through a persistent-homology construction that retains point correspondence, then regularize an autoencoder with the resulting symmetric topology divergence.
method.mechanism: A cross-distance matrix makes two copies of corresponding samples interact in a filtration. Persistence intervals that appear in the cross construction but not in the ordinary filtration quantify lost, introduced, or displaced structure. The RTD loss aggregates these intervals in both source-to-latent directions and propagates their piecewise-smooth dependence on selected pairwise distances through the encoder.
assumptions: Source and representation samples have a known one-to-one correspondence because both are views of the same mini-batch.
Finite point-cloud persistence is an adequate proxy for the topology of the underlying data manifold.
Mini-batch estimates expose the globally relevant features often enough for stochastic optimization.
The reconstruction term and warm start keep the encoder away from degenerate geometries while the topological term is introduced.

techniques.role: Measures localized persistent-topology mismatch between corresponding source and latent point clouds.
Encodes which topological features fail to transfer consistently across the two metric spaces.
Differentiates filtration birth and death edges through distances and encoder parameters.
Balances faithful reconstruction against global topological preservation.
Makes an otherwise dataset-scale topological objective usable during stochastic training.

evaluations.setting: Nested-sphere synthetic data with known nontrivial loops and voids
evaluations.metric: Recovered geometry, persistence barcodes, and RTD
evaluations.result: RTD-AE retains the intended nested structure and localizes its persistent features more faithfully than methods that preserve only neighborhoods or reconstruction.
evaluations.baseline: PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP, PHATE, ivis, plain AE, and TopoAE

evaluations.setting: Mammoth point cloud and MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and COIL-20 embeddings
evaluations.metric: Pairwise-distance correlation, triplet ranking accuracy, H0/H1 barcode Wasserstein distance, and RTD
evaluations.result: RTD-AE is broadly first or second across the global and topological metrics, with its clearest advantage at 16 latent dimensions; no method dominates every 2-D score.
evaluations.baseline: Classical, neighbor-preserving, neural, and persistent-homology dimensionality-reduction methods

evaluations.metric: The same global metric and persistence-based preservation criteria
evaluations.result: The method preserves coarse global organization and topology competitively without labels, extending beyond visual benchmarks.
evaluations.baseline: PCA and common nonlinear visualization methods

evaluations.metric: Training-time multiplier as mini-batch size increases
evaluations.result: The reported RTD overhead rises from about 1.5x at batch size 8 to approximately 4--6x at batch size 512; a COIL-20 run is reported at about 20 minutes versus 10 minutes for the plain AE.

limitations: The empirical study is moderate in scale and does not establish behavior for modern high-dimensional foundation-model representations.
Persistent-homology computation sharply constrains batch size and homology degree; most experiments optimize only degree one.
A mini-batch can omit a global cycle or create a sampling artifact, so its RTD gradient need not represent whole-dataset topology.
The theorem concerns the finite sampled metric spaces and their persistence summaries, not recovery of a unique underlying manifold or semantic equivalence.
RTD-AE sometimes sacrifices reconstruction quality and is not uniformly superior on all local or 2-D visualization metrics.
failure_modes: Sparse or biased batches can make important global features invisible and train the encoder toward inconsistent topologies across updates.
Noisy short-lived persistence intervals can dominate gradients unless filtration, sampling, and loss weighting are calibrated.
A representation may match selected persistence barcodes while distorting task-relevant local density, angles, or class semantics.
Directly optimizing coordinates without the autoencoder and reconstruction prior is slow and can settle into poor geometric configurations.
Scaling to high homology degree or large batches can exhaust memory or make persistence reduction the training bottleneck.
reusable_insights: When comparing representations, preserve sample correspondence so a topological score can distinguish a relocated feature from a genuinely matching one.
Report topology, global metric structure, local neighborhoods, and reconstruction separately; none is a sufficient proxy for the others.
Use controlled synthetic manifolds with known topology before interpreting persistence losses on unlabeled real data.
Warm-start and anneal expensive structural regularizers, and audit the variance of their mini-batch gradients.
Treat homology degree and filtration scale as part of the model specification rather than hidden evaluation choices.
open_questions: Can unbiased or low-variance estimators recover dataset-level RTD from tractable mini-batches?
Can sparse complexes, witness sets, or learned landmark selection make localized topological losses scale to millions of points?
Which downstream tasks benefit causally from preserved loops or voids rather than from correlated global-distance preservation?
How should topology preservation be defined when source and latent samples have uncertain or many-to-many correspondence?
Can RTD be extended to time-varying representations so that the births, deaths, and movement of features during training are measurable?

competitive_landscape.title: Topological Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.difference: TopoAE differentiably matches persistence-critical distances to retain multiscale connectivity; RTD adds a cross-space construction intended to match broader persistent features and their localization, and identifies cases where zero TopoAE loss is insufficient.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Metric Dimensionality Reduction with Distributed Topology
competitive_landscape.difference: DIPOLE post-processes an embedding with local metric and distributed-persistence objectives and an almost-sure convergence guarantee; RTD-AE learns an amortized encoder and uses corresponding-point cross-barcodes.

competitive_landscape.title: Connectivity-Optimized Representation Learning via Persistent Homology
competitive_landscape.difference: Hofer et al. impose a chosen latent connectivity prior for one-class learning, whereas RTD-AE tries to preserve the source space's observed topology without specifying the desired connectivity in advance.

competitive_landscape.title: A Topology Layer for Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: The topology layer is a general mechanism for differentiating persistence-based objectives across several applications; RTD contributes a particular two-representation discrepancy, its guarantees, and a dimensionality-reduction evaluation.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the principal novelty is not merely adding persistence to an autoencoder, which prior work already did, but constructing a differentiable cross-space divergence that uses known point correspondence to test both topological existence and localization. The theoretical zero-divergence guarantees and explicit counterexample to the closest TopoAE objective make that distinction substantive, although the practical evidence remains limited by persistence cost and moderate benchmark scale.
reviewer_notes: All 30 extracted pages were reviewed, including the RTD and cross-barcode definitions, guarantees and proofs, differentiation scheme, autoencoder implementation, benchmark tables, runtime analysis, ablations, and appendices. Direct competing primary records were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23. Comparative claims are deliberately qualified because several table cells favor PCA, TopoAE, or a visualization baseline even though RTD-AE is strongest overall on the authors' global/topological panel.
